# Outline

## `Outline`

```python
Outline(document: Document)
```

The document's outline as its top-level items, as `doc.outline` returns it.

Each item's `children` give the rest of the tree, and `walk`
visits every item in document order. Assigning a list of
`OutlineEntry` records to `doc.outline` replaces the outline,
and `del doc.outline` removes it. The view reads the document on every
access.

### `Outline.__getitem__`

```python
Outline.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> OutlineItem | list[OutlineItem]
```

Return a top-level item, or a list of them for a slice.

### `Outline.__len__`

```python
Outline.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of top-level items.

### `Outline.__iter__`

```python
Outline.__iter__() -> Iterator[OutlineItem]
```

Iterate over the top-level items.

### `Outline.walk`

```python
Outline.walk() -> Iterator[OutlineItem]
```

Iterate over every item in document order, each before its children.

Items stored as direct dictionaries, which no handle can name, are
left out; `entries` lists them.

### `Outline.entries`

```python
Outline.entries() -> list[OutlineEntry]
```

Return every item in document order as `OutlineEntry` records.

Assigning the list, edited or not, to `doc.outline` writes the same
outline again. Reads share the outline limits: 65,536 items or
131,072 links between them (`LimitError.code == "toc_entry_count"`),
16 MiB of title and target text (`"toc_text_size"`), and 64 levels.

## `OutlineEntry`

```python
OutlineEntry(
    level: int,
    title: str,
    destination: Target | None = None,
    *,
    color: Color | None = None,
    bold: bool = False,
    italic: bool = False,
    is_open: bool = False,
)
```

One item of an outline to write, as `doc.outline = [...]` takes it.

Levels start at 1 and grow by at most one from one entry to the next; an
entry's children are the entries of the next level that follow it.
`is_open` shows the children when the document opens.

### `OutlineEntry.page`

```python
OutlineEntry.page: int | None
```

The zero-based page of a `Destination`, else `None`.

## `OutlineItem`

```python
OutlineItem(document: Document, xref: int, generation: int)
```

A handle on one item of the outline, as `doc.outline` yields it.

Properties read the document on every access, and assigning `title`,
`destination`, `color`, `bold`, `italic`, or `is_open` edits the
item at once. A handle raises `StaleObjectError` while its item no
longer exists, as after the outline is replaced; it works again if undo
restores it.

### `OutlineItem.xref`

```python
OutlineItem.xref: int
```

The item's object number.

### `OutlineItem.obj`

```python
OutlineItem.obj: Dictionary
```

The item's dictionary in the low-level object model.

### `OutlineItem.level`

```python
OutlineItem.level: int
```

The item's depth: 1 for a top-level item.

### `OutlineItem.title`

```python
OutlineItem.title: str
```

The title shown in the viewer's outline.

Settable.

### `OutlineItem.destination`

```python
OutlineItem.destination: Target | None
```

Where the item leads, or `None`.

A destination in this document that does not name an existing page
reads as `None`, and a named destination reads as the
`Destination` that it names.

Settable.

### `OutlineItem.page`

```python
OutlineItem.page: int | None
```

The zero-based page of a `Destination`, else `None`.

### `OutlineItem.color`

```python
OutlineItem.color: Color | None
```

The title's color, or `None` for the viewer's default.

Settable.

### `OutlineItem.bold`

```python
OutlineItem.bold: bool
```

Whether the title shows in bold.

Settable.

### `OutlineItem.italic`

```python
OutlineItem.italic: bool
```

Whether the title shows in italic.

Settable.

### `OutlineItem.is_open`

```python
OutlineItem.is_open: bool
```

Whether the item's children show; `False` without children.

Assigning recounts the outline's `/Count` entries; an item without
children has no open state and refuses it.

Settable.

### `OutlineItem.children`

```python
OutlineItem.children: tuple[OutlineItem, ...]
```

The item's children in order.

### `OutlineItem.to_entry`

```python
OutlineItem.to_entry() -> OutlineEntry
```

Return the item, without its children, as an `OutlineEntry`.
